purpose: Plan Batch 42 as the Product-Agent OS instruction and tool-use compliance hardening slice after the owner observed that installed Product-Agent OS mechanisms are not automatically engaged.
source_context: Owner request to add the Product-Agent OS compliance/tool-use audit requirements as Batch 42 in Track 10.
Prior local audit found the Product-Agent OS bundle installed with more skills than the active session exposed.
Prior local audit found Product-Agent OS skill agents configured with allow_implicit_invocation=false.
Prior local audit found meta instruction/tool-use prompts can route to generic bug rescue instead of Product-Agent OS lifecycle/learning-loop paths.
Prior local audit found system-file hygiene still has secret_like_literal findings requiring triage or accepted-gap handling.
non_goals: Do not turn every Product-Agent OS skill into implicit invocation without a risk-ranked policy.
Do not mutate user-level Codex config, installed plugin cache, target workspaces, hooks, automations, provider/API state, git state or external systems from this planning matrix alone.
Do not treat a fresh-session exposure check as proof of task behavior unless route and transcript/eval evidence also exists.
Do not promote self-learning-loop output to automatic skill, prompt, rule, hook or automation changes without owner approval and rollback evidence.

tasks.task: Freeze Batch 42 compliance requirements and approval boundaries.
tasks.scope: Convert the owner audit request into requirements, non-goals, source policy, approval boundaries and explicit success criteria.
tasks.codex_does: Document the Batch 42 scope, keep it planned-only, and map each requirement to the exact Track 10 source artifact.
tasks.user_does: Confirm whether Batch 42 should later execute as a local source-tree fix, an installed-cache refresh, a global Codex policy change, or only a read-only audit.
tasks.technical_value: Prevents implicit tool-use fixes from becoming unbounded config or plugin-cache mutation.
tasks.product_value: The owner gets a concrete compliance backlog instead of an ambiguous complaint about missing automation.
tasks.acceptance: Track 10 plan and source matrix state that Batch 42 is planned-only, list all approval-bound surfaces, and separate source-tree changes from installed-cache/global-session behavior.
tasks.risks_approval_gates: No execution, cache write, global config write, browser/provider/git/external action or automation activation follows from this row.

tasks.task: Build physical bundle, installed cache and active-session skill exposure inventory.
tasks.scope: Compare checked-in plugin source, user plugin cache, active session skill registry, plugin manifest and per-skill agent metadata.
tasks.codex_does: Run read-only inventory commands, normalize counts and record which Product-Agent OS skills are physically installed versus exposed in the current session.
tasks.user_does: Restart or open a fresh session only if active-session exposure cannot be validated inside the current runtime.
tasks.technical_value: Turns the suspected auto-engagement failure into a reproducible source/cache/session delta.
tasks.product_value: The owner can see whether the problem is packaging, cache refresh, session loading or routing policy.
tasks.acceptance: Evidence packet lists each Product-Agent OS skill, source path, cache path, manifest entry, agent metadata and active-session exposure status.
tasks.verification: `validate_codex_compatibility.py`, read-only file inventory, fresh-session manual proof when needed.
tasks.risks_approval_gates: Installed cache mutation or global config edits require separate exact approval.

tasks.task: Verify current official OpenAI/Codex documentation for plugins, skills, instructions and tool routing.
tasks.scope: Check official OpenAI/Codex docs before making claims about supported automatic skill/plugin behavior, instruction hierarchy, MCP/tool use and restart/session reload requirements.
tasks.codex_does: Use official docs as source truth, record source links and separate verified product behavior from local inference.
tasks.user_does: Approve any follow-up that would change global Codex settings, installed plugin state or project trust/approval policy.
tasks.technical_value: Prevents local reverse-engineering from being mistaken for official Codex behavior.
tasks.product_value: The owner receives a compliance plan that aligns with the supported product surface.
tasks.acceptance: Source registry or Batch 42 packet records official-source status, checked date, supported claims, unsupported claims and local-inference gaps.
tasks.verification: Docs source check, source registry/docs tests if claims are added to public docs, and completion-skeptic unsupported-claim review.
tasks.risks_approval_gates: Official docs may not expose every app internals detail; unresolved behavior must stay as local inference or accepted gap.

tasks.task: Define Product-Agent OS implicit invocation policy.
tasks.scope: Decide explicit-only versus narrow router-only implicit invocation for Product-Agent OS skills, with risk classes and forbidden automatic surfaces.
tasks.codex_does: Draft a policy that names which skills may be implicit, which must remain explicit, and what prompts should route to lifecycle, discovery, compliance or learning-loop paths.
tasks.user_does: Choose the policy mode before any `allow_implicit_invocation` or router default changes are implemented.
tasks.technical_value: Fixes the likely auto-engagement root cause without blindly enabling every skill.
tasks.product_value: The owner gets predictable Product-Agent OS engagement on relevant requests while approval-heavy actions remain controlled.
tasks.acceptance: Policy lists safe implicit triggers, explicit-only skills, stop conditions, approval gates and rollback path.
tasks.verification: Policy review, fixture route tests, transcript evals and no-unapproved-actions proof.
tasks.risks_approval_gates: Broad implicit invocation can over-trigger skills, add latency or bypass user intent; config/cache changes need separate approval.

tasks.task: Add a validator for Product-Agent OS skill agent metadata and implicit-invocation policy.
tasks.scope: Validate `skills/*/agents/openai.yaml`, manifest skill entries, implicit invocation flags, explicit-only gates and policy exceptions.
tasks.codex_does: Implement or specify a focused validator that fails unknown, missing or policy-inconsistent skill agent metadata.
tasks.user_does: Approve implementation of the validator when Batch 42 moves from planning to execution.
tasks.technical_value: Makes future skill exposure and invocation policy drift detectable by deterministic tests.
tasks.product_value: The owner no longer has to notice missing auto-engagement manually.
tasks.acceptance: Validator reports all Product-Agent OS skills, policy class, implicit flag, route owner and actionable errors without exposing secrets or raw private paths.
tasks.verification: Focused validator tests, Codex compatibility validation, fixture eval field if promoted.
tasks.risks_approval_gates: Validator must not rewrite metadata automatically or mutate installed cache.

tasks.task: Validate fresh-session skill registry exposure after any source or cache change.
tasks.scope: Prove whether a new Codex session exposes the full Product-Agent OS skill set and whether stale current-session behavior remains expected.
tasks.codex_does: Prepare the exact smoke checklist and compare old-session versus fresh-session evidence.
tasks.user_does: Start a fresh Codex session or restart the app when requested because active skill loading cannot always be refreshed in-place.
tasks.technical_value: Separates source correctness from stale runtime/session loading.
tasks.product_value: The owner knows whether a fix is active in real use, not only present on disk.
tasks.acceptance: Fresh-session packet records exposed skills, missing skills, plugin version, restart requirement and accepted gaps.
tasks.verification: Fresh-session manual proof plus docs/control-plane sync; no runtime claim from old-session evidence alone.
tasks.risks_approval_gates: Current session may remain stale; do not claim fixed auto-engagement until fresh-session proof exists.

tasks.task: Add runtime routing tests for instruction/tool-use audit and Product-Agent OS compliance prompts.
tasks.scope: Cover prompts such as instruction compliance audit, tool-use compliance, Product-Agent OS auto-engagement failure, and self-learning-loop request.
tasks.codex_does: Add route fixtures/transcripts that fail if these prompts route only to generic bug rescue or ordinary implementation paths.
tasks.user_does: Review the expected first response style: audit-first, plan-first, learning-loop candidate, or direct implementation when safe.
tasks.technical_value: Prevents meta-compliance requests from being swallowed by generic bug triage.
tasks.product_value: The owner sees the installed Product-Agent OS workflow engage when they explicitly ask for it.
tasks.acceptance: Runtime route packet recommends Product-Agent OS discovery/lifecycle/compliance/learning-loop handling and records why `bug_rescue` is insufficient when used alone.
tasks.verification: `test_codex_runtime_runner_state_routes`, transcript evals, behavioral eval fixtures and no-provider/no-browser/no-git proof.
tasks.risks_approval_gates: Route recommendation is not permission to mutate config, cache, target files or external systems.

tasks.task: Add tool-use and instruction-compliance eval cases.
tasks.scope: Evaluate whether the agent reads required Product-Agent OS skills, obeys project/global instruction hierarchy, uses official docs for OpenAI/Codex claims, and keeps approval boundaries.
tasks.codex_does: Create deterministic cases and expected terms for skill loading, official-doc source status, no-unapproved-actions proof and completion-skeptic second pass.
tasks.user_does: Provide additional real prompts that previously failed, if available, so they can become regression cases.
tasks.technical_value: Turns observed instruction/tool-use drift into repeatable regression coverage.
tasks.product_value: The owner can verify that the workflow improves across future sessions rather than relying on memory.
tasks.acceptance: Eval set catches missing skill reads, unsupported official-doc claims, route bypass, missing approval gates and false completion claims.
tasks.verification: Behavioral evals, transcript replay, focused docs tests and completion-skeptic review.
tasks.risks_approval_gates: Eval fixtures must not include raw private chat logs, secrets or user-specific absolute paths.

tasks.task: Route self-learning-loop through staged metrics and lessons only.
tasks.scope: Use `agent_skill_metrics_loop` and learning-loop packets to capture failures, lessons and candidate durable rules without auto-applying changes.
tasks.codex_does: Record failure patterns, candidate rules, eval follow-ups and ownership without activating hooks, schedules or automatic skill rewrites.
tasks.user_does: Approve any later durable-rule, skill, plugin, config, hook or automation change separately.
tasks.technical_value: Provides a safe learning loop that improves evidence without mutating policy automatically.
tasks.product_value: The owner gets continuous improvement proposals without hidden self-modification.
tasks.acceptance: Learning-loop packet lists incidents, lessons, candidate changes, evidence, owner decision needed and rollback/disable path; auto-apply is false.
tasks.verification: Metrics-loop tests, automation-policy tests, no-active-automation proof and docs/control-plane sync.
tasks.risks_approval_gates: No automatic memory write, skill rewrite, hook activation, automation schedule or global rule change.

tasks.task: Triage system-file hygiene and secret-like literal findings.
tasks.scope: Review Product-Agent OS system-file hygiene findings, especially secret-like literals, and classify real issues, synthetic fixtures, policy literals and accepted gaps.
tasks.codex_does: Run focused hygiene checks, avoid echoing sensitive values, and produce remediation or accepted-gap records.
tasks.user_does: Approve any canonical file edits if a real secret, policy change or fixture rewrite is needed.
tasks.technical_value: Removes or classifies compliance blockers that can hide real instruction/tool-use readiness.
tasks.product_value: The owner gets a cleaner trust boundary for plugin packaging and internal use.
tasks.acceptance: Hygiene packet records finding counts, classes, fix/accept decisions, no-secret disclosure policy and next action.
tasks.verification: `validate_system_file_hygiene.py`, focused tests, docs/source sync and diff hygiene.
tasks.risks_approval_gates: Do not print secret-like raw values; real secret remediation may require out-of-band owner action.

tasks.task: Close Batch 42 with docs/control-plane sync and no-unapproved-actions proof.
tasks.scope: Synchronize Track 10 plan/backlog, root control-plane files, test/eval pointers and final residual risks after execution.
tasks.codex_does: Write the closure packet only after actual checks run, then separate supported claims, unsupported claims, accepted gaps and next approvals.
tasks.user_does: Decide whether the result should remain manual-only, proceed to cache refresh, proceed to global config changes, or become a release candidate.
tasks.technical_value: Prevents planning matrix presence from being mistaken for Product-Agent OS auto-engagement being fixed.
tasks.product_value: The owner receives a clean go/no-go decision and next approval list.
tasks.acceptance: Closure records implemented rows, current verification evidence, fresh-session status, route/eval results, residual risks and exact next approvals.
tasks.verification: Focused Batch 42 tests, `validate_codex_compatibility.py`, runtime route tests, `python -m unittest tests.product_agent_os.test_product_agent_os_docs -v`, `python tools\check_docs.py`, `git diff --check` and fresh-session proof if required.
tasks.risks_approval_gates: No release, cache refresh, global config write, target mutation, provider call, browser automation, git action, external write or automation activation without separate approval.

suggested_order: B42-S1 scope, inventory and official-source check
B42-S2 implicit invocation policy, validator and fresh-session exposure proof
B42-S3 runtime route and instruction/tool-use eval hardening
B42-S4 staged self-learning-loop and system-file hygiene triage
B42-S5 closure, control-plane sync and no-unapproved-actions proof
